title: Session Templates Garden — personal sketch and rough PRD
body:
High level idea

Problem statement: Teams build the same conversational flows repeatedly (onboarding flows, troubleshooting helpers, sales discovery prompts). Right now people copy-paste prompt blocks into new sessions, tweak parameters, then forget what worked. We need a lightweight first-class way for users to create, discover, and reuse session 'templates' inside the product — including parameterized inputs, tags, small metadata, and quick previews.

Why this is useful
- Reduces duplication and onboarding friction for power users
- Encourages best-practice prompt composition and safer defaults
- Enables measurable quality & cost improvements (reusable prompts lower dev iteration time)

Goals (minimal viable scope)
1) Template composer in Console: allow user to save current session as a template with name, description, tags, and optional parameter placeholders.
2) Template library: browse personal + org templates, filter by tag, search by name/text, quick preview of last-run example.
3) Parameterization: define up to 8 placeholders with optional type hint (string, number, enum) and default values. Composer should inject placeholders into prompt blocks.
4) Apply & specialize: when starting a new session from template, user can fill parameters or choose 'randomize' for testing.
5) Basic versioning: store a small changelog (author, timestamp, note) for template edits.

Non-goals for v1
- Full sharing/permissions model across teams (org-private vs public) — default to personal + opt-in org share
- Rich templating language or conditional branches (Jinja-like)
- Analytics dashboards tied to templates (save for v2)

User stories
- As a developer integrating a help-bot, I want to save my multi-step troubleshooting prompt sequence so I can reuse it across product pages. Acceptance: "Save as template" creates template visible under personal library and can be applied to a new session.
- As a docs engineer, I want to parameterize the user name and product plan in the template so one template works for many customers. Acceptance: template shows placeholders, UI prompts to enter values on apply, placeholders are replaced in the session.
- As an ops lead, I want a quick preview of a template's most recent run to sanity-check outputs before applying. Acceptance: library row shows last-run snippet and timestamp.

Functional spec (rough)
- Composer workflow: Session -> Actions menu -> Save as template -> modal with fields: name, short description (140 char), tags (comma), visibility (Personal | Org opt-in), placeholders list (add/remove), default values, note. Save creates template id.
- Storage model: small JSON blob: {title, desc, blocks: [prompt_block1, ...], placeholders: [{name,type,default}], metadata}. (backend team: minimal schema, keep compact to avoid large storage).
- Apply flow: New session -> Templates -> select -> preview -> fill placeholders -> Create session.
- UI/UX: list cards, compact rows for quick pick. Hover preview with last-run output. Quick 'use defaults' checkbox.

Metrics to track (v1)
- # templates created per MAU
- % of sessions originated from a template
- Reduction in prompt-edit cycle time (survey/qual)

Rough wireframe (verbal)
- Template library: 2-column grid, left filter rail (tags, owner), top search. Each card: title, 2-line description, tags, last-run timestamp, actions [Preview | Use | Edit].
- Composer modal: split view, left shows live prompt blocks with annotated placeholders, right shows placeholder editor list. Save/Cancel.

Edge cases + constraints
- Templates containing secrets/PII: disallow saving variables marked as secret; show a warning if prompt text resembles an API key or email address pattern.
- Large sessions with many message turns — cap template size (e.g., 32KB) and warn on save.
- Backwards compatibility: when loading older template, map missing placeholder defaults to empty string.

Risk & mitigation
- Confusion between templates and saved sessions. Mitigate with clear naming, tooltip explanation, and example templates onboarding flow.
- Template drift: templates get stale. Mitigate by 'last-run' indicator and encourage owners to update.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (internal): feature behind flag for small set of power users (devtools, SEs). Gather qualitative feedback.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable for all orgs with template library, but default visibility personal. Monitor usage.
- Phase 2: org-sharing, template curated gallery, analytics.

Implementation notes for eng
- Backend: simple templates service with REST endpoints: POST /templates, GET /templates?owner=, GET /templates/{id}, PUT /templates/{id}, DELETE /templates/{id}. Use existing metadata store (Dynamo-like) and object store for larger blobs. Keep template size throttle.
- Frontend: React components in Console repo. Reuse existing session editor components to prefill blocks. Add modal + library page.
- Permissions: v1 only allow owner edits; org admins can request transfer.

Open questions (to discuss)
- Do we allow templating of function calls / tool calls? (Security and surface area concerns).
- Should templates accept 'live data' tokens (current user, time) that auto-resolve on apply? Pros: convenience. Cons: surprising outputs.
- How do templates interact with model version pinning? Should template save model config or be model-agnostic?

Example template (toy)
Title: "Customer onboarding — guided tour"
Description: Small onboarding assistant that asks 3 config questions and returns a plan.
Blocks:
- System: "You are a helpful onboarding assistant for Acme product."
- User: "Customer name: {{customer_name}} | Product plan: {{plan}} | Priority: {{priority}}\nWrite a 3-step getting-started plan tailored to the customer and plan."
Placeholders: customer_name (string, default: "New Customer"), plan (enum: [free, pro, enterprise], default: "free"), priority (enum: [low, med, high], default: "med").

Quick experiments to run with early users
- In-product template gallery vs local 'save to file' UX: which is more discoverable?
- Measure friction: time from 'save as template' to 'apply' for users vs baseline.
- Test parameter UI: inline replacements vs modal form — which one reduces mistakes?

Notes to self
- Talk to Mika about analytics schema (are we comfortable capturing template_id on request logs?).
- Ask infra about a soft quota for template storage per user.
- Draft short onboarding email + in-console tooltip for first 2 weeks after rollout.
- Keep this doc light; will convert to Confluence when aligned with PM/Eng.

-- end --
